html:
Jan van Eyck was a painter who worked in Bruges for the Duke of Burgundy and died there in 1441. He was the greatest of the early Flemish painters and a master of oil paint.

He did not invent oil painting, but he used layers of thin, clear oil glaze to reach a new richness of light, colour and detail. With his brother Hubert he made the Ghent Altarpiece, finished in 1432, one of the most famous works in Europe. His Arnolfini Portrait of 1434, with its mirror and its signature on the wall, is one of the first portraits of ordinary people in their home.

Painters across Europe, in Italy too, learned from the Flemish oil technique. His world was the rich court of the Burgundian dukes and the merchant city of Bruges. Later painters of the Low Countries, from Bruegel to Rembrandt, built on his realism. See Belgium.
